THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA  ORAL ORDER Petitioner-accused No.4 is before this Court seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against her in C.C.No.10478/2022 pending on the file of the learned XXXVII ACMM, Bengaluru,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498(A) and 504 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC') and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, in Crime No. 242/2021 of Basavanagudi Women Police Station.
NC: 2024:KHC:45892 2.

Heard Sri.Madhav B Kashyap, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt. Rashmi Jadhav,
learned Additional SPP for the respondent No.1 for the State.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 is absent.
No representation.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
Smt Pavithra R vs State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87502659/
2 "Whether the petitioner has made out any grounds to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against her?"

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn my attention to the decree dated 08.07.2024 passed in MC No.3105/2021 on the file of the learned VIth Additional Prl.Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru,
dissolving the marriage of respondent No.2 herein with accused No.1.
He has also drawn the attention of the Court to the memorandum of settlement under Section 89 of Cr.PC filed in MC No.3105/2021.
As per NC: 2024:KHC:45892 clause 6(a) of memorandum of settlement, respondent No.2 had agreed to cooperate to close or quash the criminal proceedings in CC No.10478/2022.

When it is stated that accused No.1 is the husband of respondent No.2 and he entered into settlement with the complainant and the criminal proceedings against the main accused i.e., accused No.1 is agreed to be quashed, I do not find any reason for not extending such benefit to the petitioner.
Hence, I deem it appropriate to allow the petition.

5. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the Affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The petition is allowed.
(ii) The entire proceedings in Crime No.242/2021, pending in CC No.10478/2022 on the file of the learned XXXVII ACMM, Bengaluru, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 504 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, is hereby quashed against the petitioner.
NC: 2024:KHC:45892
In view of the disposal of the main petition pending IA stands No.1/2024 is disposed of.

Sd/-
